invariants: Original NSMatrix/NSButtonCell determine pointer selection, disabled-member actions, outside release, focus/key-cell state and multiple click handling. The unchanged NativeUI provider and API 520 are reused. No control drawing, layout or tracking policy is copied.

Shared RadioBinding stores native typed completion state, consumes actions once and forwards original click counts through existing counted-press transport. Frame retirement ends native mouseDown before changing models; the shared host cancels a queued press that has not started.

Chromium calls its original MouseEventManager::DispatchMouseEvent with the native action target, preserving PointerEvent construction and all original pointer-source arguments. Node publicly inherits EventTarget in the pinned source. Original radio preactivation and cancellation remain browser-owned.

Firefox calls its original EventStateManager::DispatchClickEvents. Guarded PreHandleEvent captures original radio identity before page callbacks; retained semantic references and context retirement preserve cancellation when frames disappear or nodes change type. A post-mouseup fallback uses the same original click dispatcher when no ordinary engine click target exists.

Both adapters use original canonical grouping and revalidate current frame/binding identity, membership, type and enabled state after callbacks. Focus restoration reads the real original engine focus state; the same helpers serve key and pointer transactions.

The provider, loader, scrollbar shim, both installed browser executables, AppKit and 20 measured production runtime files are unchanged. Only separate small adapters were compiled, and shared bridge/host source changed. Browser toolbar, address bar and tabs stay original.
